title: Grandmother's Chicken Biryani
description: A fragrant, layered rice dish slow-cooked with tender chicken, fried onions, and whole spices. A festive weekend classic.

blocks.alt: A highly aromatic pot of hot chicken biryani with long grain rice

blocks.text: This is the biryani I grew up eating on Sundays. My grandmother would spend hours frying onions, soaking basmati rice, and layering it with chicken marinated in warm yogurt and spices. It's truly a labor of love.

items.text: Marinate the chicken pieces in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, chili powder, and salt. Set aside for at least 1 hour.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry the sliced onions until brown and caramelized. Remove half for layering later.
Add the marinated chicken to the pot with the remaining onions and cook until the chicken is tender and the oil separates.
In a separate pot, cook the soaked basmati rice in salted water with whole spices until it is 70% cooked. Drain the rice.
Layer the cooked chicken with mint, cilantro, caramelized onions, and the partially cooked rice. Drizzle melted ghee and saffron water on top.
Cover the pot tightly (traditionally sealed with dough) and cook on very low heat ('dum') for 20 minutes to let the steam infuse.

blocks.text: Always use aged long-grain basmati rice for that perfect, non-sticky texture where every grain is separate.
